# Bar Plots {#ggplot2-bar-plot}

## Introduction

:::{.callout-note}
## Why this chart

Bars encode amounts with length, making comparisons across categories instant.
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
## Common pitfall

Truncating the value axis exaggerates differences; start bars at zero unless you say otherwise.
:::

In this chapter, we will learn to:

- build 
    - simple bar plot
    - stacked bar plot
    - grouped bar plot
    - proportional bar plot
- map aesthetics to variables
- specify values for 
    - bar color
    - bar line color
    - bar line type
    - bar line size

```{r bar, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
```

## Data

```{r import201, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE}
ecom <- read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rsquaredacademy/datasets/master/ecom.csv',
  col_types = list(col_factor(levels = c('Desktop', 'Mobile', 'Tablet')), 
  col_logical(), col_logical(), 
  col_factor(levels = c('Affiliates', 'Direct', 'Display', 'Organic', 'Paid', 'Referral', 'Social'))))
ecom
```

### Data Dictionary

- device: device used to visit the website
- bouncers: whether visit was a bouncer (exit website from landing page)
- purchase: whether visitor purchased
- referrer: referrer website/search engine


## Basic Plot

We can create a bar plot using `geom_bar()`. It takes a single input, a 
categorical variable. In the example below, we plot the number of visits for 
each device type. 

```{r bar2, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device))
```

## Bar Color

We can modify the color of the bars using the `fill` argument. In the example
below, we assign different colors to the 3 bars in the plot. If you use the
`color` argument, it modifies the color of the bar line, not the 
background color of the bars. We will look at that later in the chapter.

```{r bar3, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device), fill = c('red', 'blue', 'green'))
```

## Stacked Bar Plot

If you want to look at the distribution of one categorical variable across the
levels of another categorical variable, you can create a stacked bar plot. In
ggplot2, we create a stacked bar plot by mapping the `fill` argument to the
second categorical variable. In the example below, we have mapped `fill` to 
the `referrer` variable. 

```{r bar7, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device, fill = referrer))
```

## Grouped Bar Plot

Grouped bar plots are a variation of stacked bar plots. Instead of being 
stacked on top of one another, the bars are placed next to one another and 
grouped by levels. In the example below, we create a grouped bar plot and you
can observe that the bars are placed next to one another instead of being 
stacked. To create a grouped bar plot, use the `position` argument and set it
to `'dodge'`. 

```{r bar8, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device, fill = referrer), position = 'dodge')
```

## Proportional Bar Plot

In a proportional bar plot, all the bars have the same height. To create a
proportional bar plot, use the `position` argument and set it to `'fill'`.

```{r bar10, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device, fill = referrer), position = 'fill')
```

## Horizontal Bar Plot

We can create a horizontal bar plot by flipping the coordinate axes of a 
regular plot. To flip the axes, use `coord_flip()` as shown below.

```{r bar9, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device, fill = referrer)) +
  coord_flip()
```

## Bar Line 

We can modify the color of the bar line using the `color` argument. Specify the
color using its name or hex code.

```{r bar4, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device), fill = 'white', color = c('red', 'blue', 'green'))
```

To modify the line type of the bar line, use the `linetype` argument. It takes
values between `0` and `6`.

```{r bar5, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device), fill = 'white',  color = 'black', linetype = 2)
```

We can modify the width of the bar line using the `linewidth` argument. It takes
any value greater than `0`.

```{r bar6, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(ecom) +
  geom_bar(aes(device), fill = 'white', color = 'black', linewidth = 2)
```

## Exercises

1. Draw counts of cars per cylinder class from `mtcars`.
2. Group by gears with dodged bars, gap tuned via `position_dodge(width = 0.8)`.
3. Rewrite the plot with a message-first title; keep bars starting at zero.
